items_missed: Almost no discovery. He took the customer's volunteered inventory list and booked off it — never asked about the garage/storage/balcony, walk distance, hallway or stairwell access, packing needs, box count, storage stops, additional stops, or whether there's elevator access. On a second-floor carry-down of a bed, dresser, couch, love seat, chair, TV, TV stand, and desk, elevator vs. stairs alone is the single biggest time driver and it was never asked.

No estimate was ever built. He quoted the $510 minimum as the price and stopped — no typical time range for the job, no 'here's what could push it longer,' no upper bound. The customer walked away believing $510 is the number.

Clock section scored zero. He framed the minimum purely as a dollar figure ('the minimum starts at $510') and never said 2.5 hours, never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, never explained 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, and never sense-checked.
Never listed what's included — no gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, or tools.
Never mentioned disassembly/reassembly is included, despite a bed, desk, and TV stand in the inventory.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch at all.
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage or the 60c/lb baseline.

Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee — and this is the call where it mattered most: he gave a 12:30-2:30 arrival window and said another move is scheduled ahead of it, then offered no guarantee against that window slipping.
No Save Your Ass prep speech.
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener, no agenda statement, no 'sound good?', no 'how are you today?'
Never asked 'Any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave business hours or how to reach us.
Confirmation email mentioned but not explained — no bolded key details at the top, no 'reply with any corrections.'
Never used the customer's name — she introduced herself as Tanya in her first sentence and he never said it once.
Garbled/confusing delivery on the two most important numbers: 'the minimum of $2 is anywhere from $510 to 510' and an afternoon window quoted as '12:30 AM to 2:30 PM.'
top_strength: He handled the price objection with real integrity. When Tanya pushed back hard ('Am I calling the right Einstein moving? You only charged us $300 last time'), he didn't argue or discount — he pulled her email, found the April invoice, and showed her the actual $475 she paid against the then-rate of $190/hr. That factual correction turned a near-walk into a booking inside 30 seconds.
coaching_note: Jules booked the move but skipped the entire scorecard to get there — no discovery, no clock explanation, no differentiators, and no time estimate. He quoted $510 as the price rather than as the floor, which is exactly the pattern driving the estimate-accuracy gap: if this 8-item second-floor carry-down runs past 2.5 hours, the customer was never told that was possible. Even on a fast repeat-customer booking, the 2.5 hour minimum + 15-minute increments + a realistic time range are non-negotiable.
phone_presence_notes: Pleasant and easygoing ('No problem,' 'Got it,' 'Awesome') and he kept a repeat B2B customer happy through a price objection, but there was zero name use, no empathy language when she expressed sticker shock, and no relationship-building with an account that has moved with Einstein before.
audio_review_reason: Short call with several garbled passages on load-bearing details ('the minimum of $2 is anywhere from $510 to 510', '12:30 AM to 2:30 PM', 'same Publix'). Need audio to confirm whether the clarity deduction reflects the rep's actual delivery or is transcription noise, and to verify the arrival window he actually quoted.
